sql: SELECT SUM((oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) - o.discount_amount - COALESCE(r.refund_amount, 0)) AS net_revenue FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT order_id, SUM(refund_amount) AS refund_amount FROM refunds GROUP BY order_id) r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE c.is_test = false AND o.status = 'completed' AND CAST(o.ordered_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes' AS DATE) >= DATE '2026-03-01' AND CAST(o.ordered_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes' AS DATE) <= DATE '2026-03-31'
assumptions: Refunds on completed orders are aggregated per order and subtracted once as per net_revenue definition.

sql: SELECT round(avg((item_totals.item_total - o.discount_amount))::numeric, 2) AS aov_card FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN (SELECT order_id, sum(quantity * unit_price) AS item_total FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) item_totals ON o.order_id = item_totals.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND o.payment_method = 'card' AND c.is_test = false
assumptions: AOV is rounded to 2 decimal places as requested.

sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT o.customer_id) AS customer_count FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.is_test = false AND o.status = 'completed' AND cast((o.ordered_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes') AS date) BETWEEN '2026-09-01' AND '2026-09-30'
assumptions: Last 30 days relative to 2026-09-30 inclusive of both ends refers to the period from 2026-09-01 to 2026-09-30.

sql: WITH customer_first_order AS (SELECT c.customer_id, MIN(CAST(o.ordered_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes' AS DATE)) AS first_order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.is_test = false AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id) SELECT count(customer_id) AS new_customers FROM customer_first_order WHERE first_order_date >= DATE '2026-08-01' AND first_order_date <= DATE '2026-08-31'

SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN o.status = 'returned' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) / NULLIF(SUM(CASE WHEN o.status IN ('completed', 'returned') THEN 1 ELSE 0 END), 0), 4) AS return_rate FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.is_test = false AND o.status IN ('completed', 'returned') AND CAST(o.ordered_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes' AS DATE) BETWEEN DATE '2026-09-30' - INTERVAL '89 days' AND DATE '2026-09-30'

WITH ist_orders AS (SELECT o.order_id, o.status, CAST(o.ordered_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes' AS DATE) AS ist_date FROM orders o INNER JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE c.is_test = false AND o.status IN ('completed', 'cancelled', 'returned')) SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN status = 'cancelled' THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) / COUNT(*), 4) AS cancellation_rate FROM ist_orders WHERE ist_date >= DATE '2026-09-01' AND ist_date <= DATE '2026-09-30'
assumptions: This month refers to September 2026 as defined by the relative periods rule for the as-of date 2026-09-30.

sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT t1.order_id) AS orders_count FROM orders AS t1 INNER JOIN customers AS t2 ON t1.customer_id = t2.customer_id WHERE (t2.is_test = false OR t2.is_test IS NULL) AND cast(t1.ordered_at + interval '5 hours 30 minutes' AS date) = date '2026-02-09'
assumptions: Orders placed on 9 February 2026 refers to IST date as per reporting timezone rule

sql: SELECT COUNT(o.order_id) AS completed_orders FROM orders AS o JOIN customers AS c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE (c.is_test IS NULL OR c.is_test = FALSE) AND o.status = 'completed' AND CAST(o.ordered_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes' AS DATE) >= DATE '2026-05-01' AND CAST(o.ordered_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes' AS DATE) <= DATE '2026-05-31'
assumptions: May 2026 is interpreted in IST as dates from 2026-05-01 to 2026-05-31 inclusive.

sql: SELECT sum(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS gmv FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.is_test = false AND o.status != 'cancelled' AND cast(o.ordered_at + interval '5 hours 30 minutes' as date) BETWEEN date '2026-09-30' - interval '59 days' AND date '2026-09-30'
assumptions: Last 60 days means 60 consecutive IST dates ending on 2026-09-30 inclusive, which is from 2026-08-02 to 2026-09-30.

sql: SELECT coalesce(sum(item_totals.item_total - o.discount_amount), 0) - coalesce(sum(r.refund_amount), 0) AS customer_ltv FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT order_id, sum(quantity * unit_price) AS item_total FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) item_totals ON o.order_id = item_totals.order_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT order_id, sum(refund_amount) AS refund_amount FROM refunds GROUP BY order_id) r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE c.customer_id = 2296 AND c.is_test = false AND o.status = 'completed'
assumptions: Customer lifetime value uses net revenue per order calculated as item total minus discount minus refunds on completed orders.

sql: WITH customer_revenue AS (SELECT c.customer_id, COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 0) - COALESCE(MAX(o.discount_amount), 0) - COALESCE(MAX(r.refund_amount), 0) AS ltv FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id AND o.status = 'completed' LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id LEFT JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE c.is_test = false GROUP BY c.customer_id) SELECT COUNT(customer_id) AS customer_count FROM customer_revenue WHERE ltv > 15000
assumptions: Orders with status completed are the only orders included in customer lifetime value calculation as per metric:customer_ltv rule.

sql: SELECT round(cast(sum(case when completed_orders >= 2 then 1 else 0 end) as double) / count(*), 4) as fraction_repeat FROM (SELECT c.customer_id, count(case when o.status = 'completed' then 1 end) as completed_orders FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.is_test = false GROUP BY c.customer_id HAVING count(case when o.status = 'completed' then 1 end) >= 1)
assumptions: Completed orders mean orders with status = 'completed'.

sql: WITH first_completed_orders AS (SELECT c.customer_id, c.acquisition_channel, MIN(CAST(o.ordered_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes' AS DATE)) AS first_order_date FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.is_test = false AND o.status = 'completed' GROUP BY c.customer_id, c.acquisition_channel), first_order_per_customer AS (SELECT customer_id, acquisition_channel, ROW_NUMBER() OVER (PARTITION BY customer_id ORDER BY first_order_date ASC) as rn FROM first_completed_orders), customer_first_channel AS (SELECT customer_id, acquisition_channel FROM first_order_per_customer WHERE rn = 1) SELECT acquisition_channel AS channel, COUNT(customer_id) AS new_customers FROM customer_first_channel GROUP BY acquisition_channel ORDER BY new_customers DESC LIMIT 1
assumptions: If a customer has their first completed orders on different days through different channels (unlikely), we pick the earliest channel, but normally a customer is tied to one acquisition channel.

sql: SELECT o.payment_method, ROUND(AVG(CAST(sub.item_total - o.discount_amount AS DECIMAL(10,2))), 2) AS aov FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN (SELECT order_id, SUM(quantity * unit_price) AS item_total FROM order_items GROUP BY order_id) sub ON o.order_id = sub.order_id WHERE o.status = 'completed' AND c.is_test = false GROUP BY o.payment_method

SELECT ROUND(CAST(SUM(CASE WHEN oi.category = 'electronics' THEN oi.quantity * oi.unit_price ELSE 0 END) AS DOUBLE) / SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price), 4) AS electronics_gmv_share FROM order_items oi JOIN orders o ON oi.order_id = o.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE (c.is_test IS NOT TRUE) AND o.status != 'cancelled'
assumptions: GMV definition includes non-cancelled orders, and the share is calculated against the total GMV.

sql: SELECT c.city, COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price - o.discount_amount - COALESCE(r.refund_sum, 0)), 0) AS net_revenue FROM customers c JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id LEFT JOIN (SELECT order_id, SUM(refund_amount) AS refund_sum FROM refunds GROUP BY order_id) r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE c.is_test = false AND o.status = 'completed' AND CAST(o.ordered_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes' AS DATE) >= DATE '2026-09-01' AND CAST(o.ordered_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes' AS DATE) <= DATE '2026-09-30' GROUP BY c.city
assumptions: Cities for customers who placed no completed orders in September 2026 are not included, as is standard for GROUP BY aggregates.

sql: SELECT ROUND(AVG(CAST(DATE_DIFF('day', CAST(c.signup_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes' AS DATE), CAST(o.ordered_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes' AS DATE)) AS DOUBLE)), 2) AS avg_days_signup_to_first_order FROM customers c JOIN (SELECT customer_id, MIN(ordered_at) AS ordered_at FROM orders WHERE status = 'completed' GROUP BY customer_id) o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id WHERE c.is_test = false
assumptions: First completed order date in IST is calculated from the minimum ordered_at timestamp among completed orders for each customer.

sql: WITH customer_ltv AS (SELECT c.customer_id, COALESCE(SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price - o.discount_amount), 0) - COALESCE(SUM(r.refund_amount), 0) AS ltv FROM customers c LEFT JOIN orders o ON c.customer_id = o.customer_id AND o.status = 'completed' LEFT JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id LEFT JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id WHERE c.is_test = false GROUP BY c.customer_id) SELECT COUNT(*) AS customer_count FROM customer_ltv WHERE ltv = 0
assumptions: Customers with no orders or only non-completed orders have an LTV of zero and are counted.

sql: SELECT count(DISTINCT o.order_id) AS returned_orders_with_refund FROM orders o JOIN refunds r ON o.order_id = r.order_id JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id WHERE o.status = 'returned' AND c.is_test = false
assumptions: Test customers and their orders are excluded as per rule:test_accounts.

sql: SELECT date_trunc('month', (o.ordered_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes'))::DATE AS month_start, SUM(oi.quantity * oi.unit_price) AS gmv FROM orders o JOIN customers c ON o.customer_id = c.customer_id JOIN order_items oi ON o.order_id = oi.order_id WHERE c.is_test = false AND o.status != 'cancelled' AND EXTRACT(YEAR FROM (o.ordered_at + INTERVAL '5 hours 30 minutes')) = 2026 GROUP BY 1 ORDER BY 1
